transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Thanks for seeing me, Dr. Smith. Lately, in long meetings and on site, my mind keeps drifting and I can’t seem to stay focused on what people are saying or what I’m supposed to be tracking. It’s really starting to impact my ability to manage these big construction projects, so I knew I needed to get some help.
Did you experience these challenges with focus, organization, or sitting still when you were a child, or is this a relatively new development in your life?

Well, they became a major crisis about two years ago when I took on these larger projects, but they actually go all the way back to when I was a kid. Even in elementary school, teachers sent notes home about me daydreaming, talking over other kids, and needing someone to stand over me just to finish my worksheets.
Beyond these issues with focus, have you been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or losing interest in activities you usually enjoy for most of the day?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or losing interest in things I enjoy. It's really more that I'm just incredibly stressed and frustrated because of how much these focus issues are screwing things up at work.
Besides having trouble focusing, do you often find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having a hard time staying seated in situations where it is expected?

Yes, definitely. In long office meetings, sitting still for an hour feels completely unbearable, so I'm constantly popping up to refill my coffee or 'check on things' in the hallway. I also get incredibly antsy, like I'm going to crawl out of my skin, whenever I have to wait around, like in line at the permit office.
Do you often find yourself acting or speaking without thinking, such as interrupting others during conversations or making impulsive decisions that you later regret?

Yes, it's honestly really embarrassing, but I constantly cut people off mid-sentence or barge into conversations because of this urgent need to speak right away. In meetings, I often blurt out answers before my boss even finishes his question, which has led to some terrible misunderstandings because I didn't actually let him finish.
